source.text: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: From where [come] wars and from where fights among you?

en.L: From where [come] wars and from where [come] fights among you?
en.B: Where do the wars and the fights among you come from?
en.R: What is causing the wars and fights among you?

es.L: ¿De dónde [vienen] guerras y de dónde [vienen] peleas entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: ¿De dónde vienen las guerras y las peleas que hay entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.R: ¿Qué es lo que causa las guerras y las peleas entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?

sw.L: Vita [vinatoka] wapi, na mapigano [yanatoka] wapi kati yenu?
sw.B: Vita vinatoka wapi, na mapigano yaliyo kati yenu yanatoka wapi?
sw.R: Ni nini kinachosababisha vita na mapigano kati yenu?

decisions.choice: wars and fights: bitter conflicts within the community, not battles between armies
decisions.reason: πόλεμος and μάχη are words for war and battle. James uses them as strong pictures for the quarrels "among you", among the believers he writes to. The same pair returns as verbs at the end of verse 2. He has just warned that jealousy and selfish ambition bring disorder (3:14-16).

decisions.choice: from where: James asks for the source, and answers in the next sentence
decisions.reason: The repeated Πόθεν asks where the conflicts come from, not only why they happen. The next sentence gives the answer: from the pleasures at war inside them. The question follows 3:18, where peace is the soil in which righteousness grows.

decisions.choice: wars ... fights
decisions.reason: Keeps the picture of war, which James carries on with "at war" in the next sentence and "you fight and you wage war" in verse 2.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: James writes to his readers in the plural throughout the letter. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Paul's letters.

source.text: οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Not from here, out of the pleasures of you that [are] warring in the members of you?

en.L: [Is it] not from here, from your pleasures that are waging war in your members?
en.B: Do they not come from here, from your pleasures that are at war inside you?
en.R: They come from your selfish desires for pleasure, which are fighting a war inside you. Is that not true?

es.L: ¿No [es] de aquí, de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} placeres que hacen guerra en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} miembros?
es.B: ¿No vienen de aquí, de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} placeres, que están en guerra dentro de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.R: Vienen de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} deseos egoístas de placer, que pelean una guerra dentro de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¿No es así?

sw.L: Je, si kutoka hapa, kutoka katika anasa zenu zinazofanya vita katika viungo vyenu?
sw.B: Je, hayatoki hapa, katika anasa zenu zinazopigana vita ndani yenu?
sw.R: Yanatoka katika tamaa zenu za kujifurahisha, ambazo zinapigana vita ndani yenu. Je, sivyo?

decisions.choice: pleasures: the craving for what pleases oneself
decisions.reason: ἡδονή is pleasure, and in the New Testament nearly always the self-seeking kind (Luke 8:14; Titus 3:3). James uses the word again in verse 3: people ask so that they can spend on their pleasures.

decisions.choice: your members: the parts of each person's body, so the war is inside each of you
alternatives: the members of the church, as if the pleasures were fighting among the believers
decisions.reason: μέλος is a limb or part of the body. Paul speaks of a law at war in his members (Romans 7:23), and Peter of desires that wage war against the soul (1 Peter 2:11). The fights among them begin as a war inside each of them.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: οὐκ at the head of the question expects agreement: yes, the fights come from there.

decisions.choice: inside you
decisions.reason: Says plainly what "in your members" means here (m2). Literal keeps the Greek picture.

decisions.choice: selfish desires for pleasure; Is that not true?
alternatives: Is it not from your pleasures?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer first and then asks for agreement, as the Greek question expects (m3). "Selfish" says what kind of pleasure is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: anasa (L, B); tamaa za kujifurahisha (R)
decisions.reason: "Anasa" is pleasure sought for oneself, often self-indulgent, which is the sense of the meaning decision; "raha" and "starehe" are neutral words for comfort and ease. Verse 3 uses "anasa" again. Readable says "desires to please yourselves".

source.text: ἐπιθυμεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε· φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε, καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν· μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε.

records.literal_gloss: You desire, and not you have; you murder and you envy, and not you are able to obtain; you fight and you wage war.

en.L: You desire, and you do not have; you murder and you envy, and you are not able to obtain; you fight and you wage war.
en.B: You crave, and you do not have. You murder and you envy, and you cannot get what you want. You fight and you wage war.
en.R: You want things, but you do not have them. You kill and you are jealous, but you still cannot get what you want. You fight and make war.

es.L: {{plural_you:Desean|Deseáis}}, y no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}; {{plural_you:asesinan|asesináis}} y {{plural_you:envidian|envidiáis}}, y no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} alcanzar; {{plural_you:pelean|peleáis}} y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} guerra.
es.B: {{plural_you:Codician|Codiciáis}}, y no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}. {{plural_you:Asesinan|Asesináis}} y {{plural_you:envidian|envidiáis}}, y no {{plural_you:consiguen|conseguís}} lo que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}}. {{plural_you:Pelean|Peleáis}} y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} la guerra.
es.R: {{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} cosas, pero no las {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}. {{plural_you:Matan|Matáis}} y {{plural_you:sienten|sentís}} envidia, pero aun así no {{plural_you:consiguen|conseguís}} lo que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}}. {{plural_you:Pelean|Peleáis}} y {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} guerra.

sw.L: Mnatamani, wala hamna; mnaua na mnaona wivu, wala hamwezi kupata; mnapigana na mnafanya vita.
sw.B: Mnatamani, lakini hamna. Mnaua na mnaona wivu, lakini hamwezi kupata mnachokitaka. Mnapigana na kufanya vita.
sw.R: Mnataka vitu, lakini hamnavyo. Mnaua na mnawaonea wengine wivu, lakini bado hamwezi kupata mnachotaka. Mnapigana na kuleta vita.

decisions.choice: three groups, as the SBLGNT punctuates them: desire without having; murder and envy without obtaining; fighting and war
alternatives: You desire and do not have, so you murder; you envy and cannot obtain, so you fight and wage war
decisions.reason: The verbs stand side by side with no word for "so" or "because". The SBLGNT groups them in three parts, each ending in frustration or conflict. Another grouping makes murder the result of frustrated desire, and fighting the result of frustrated envy. The words are the same either way; only the links between them differ.

decisions.choice: you murder: the hatred that kills, in deed or in the heart
alternatives: "you envy", a proposed correction with no manuscript support
decisions.reason: φονεύετε means "you murder". Jesus treats anger as the root of murder (Matthew 5:21-22), and 1 John 3:15 calls the one who hates a brother a murderer. James quoted the commandment against murder in 2:11 and will accuse the rich of murdering the righteous in 5:6. Because "murder" stands oddly beside "envy", some have proposed that the original word meant "you envy", but no manuscript has that reading.

decisions.choice: you envy: you are jealous of what others have
decisions.reason: ζηλόω can mean eager zeal, but here, after the "bitter jealousy" of 3:14 and 3:16, it is envy of others.

decisions.choice: you cannot get what you want
alternatives: you are not able to obtain
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object. Balanced and Readable say what they fail to obtain: what they desire.

source.text: οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Not you have because of the not to ask you;

en.L: You do not have because you do not ask.
en.B: You lack, because you do not ask.
en.R: You do not have what you need, because you do not ask God for it.

es.L: No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} porque no {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} falta, porque no {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}, porque no se lo {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} a Dios.

sw.L: Hamna kwa sababu hamwombi.
sw.B: Mnapungukiwa, kwa sababu hamwombi.
sw.R: Hamna mnachohitaji, kwa sababu hammwombi Mungu awape.

decisions.choice: ask: ask God in prayer
decisions.reason: The asking is prayer to God, as in 1:5-6, where whoever lacks wisdom is told to ask God, who gives to all generously. Verse 3 goes on to say why some prayers are not answered.

decisions.choice: what you need; ask God for it
alternatives: You do not have, because you do not ask
decisions.reason: Readable says what they lack and whom they should ask (m1).

source.text: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε, διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε, ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε.

records.literal_gloss: You ask and not you receive, because wrongly you ask, that in the pleasures of you you may spend [it].

en.L: You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend [it] on your pleasures.
en.B: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because your asking is wrong: you want to spend what you get on your pleasures.
en.R: And when you do ask God, you do not get what you ask for. That is because you ask for the wrong reasons. You want to use it only for your own pleasure.

es.L: {{plural_you:Piden|Pedís}} y no {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}}, porque {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} mal, para que [lo] {{plural_you:gasten|gastéis}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} placeres.
es.B: Y cuando {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}, no {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}}, porque {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} mal: {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} gastar lo que {{plural_you:reciban|recibáis}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} placeres.
es.R: Y cuando sí le {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} a Dios, no {{plural_you:reciben|recibís}} lo que {{plural_you:piden|pedís}}. Es porque {{plural_you:piden|pedís}} con malas intenciones. Solo {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} usarlo para {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} propio placer.

sw.L: Mnaomba wala hampokei, kwa sababu mnaomba vibaya, ili mtumie [mnachopata] kwa anasa zenu.
sw.B: Na mnapoomba, hampokei, kwa sababu mnaomba vibaya: mnataka kutumia mnachopata kwa anasa zenu.
sw.R: Na hata mnapomwomba Mungu, hampati mnachoomba. Ni kwa sababu mnaomba kwa nia mbaya. Mnataka kutumia mtakachopewa kwa kujifurahisha wenyewe tu.

decisions.choice: active and middle forms of "ask" with the same meaning
alternatives: a contrast between true prayer and self-interested asking
decisions.reason: James moves from the middle αἰτεῖσθαι (verse 2) to the active αἰτεῖτε and back to the middle αἰτεῖσθε. Some see a difference in the kind of asking, but the two forms overlap in New Testament use, and nothing else in the sentence marks a contrast.

decisions.choice: wrongly: with a wrong aim, as the purpose clause explains
decisions.reason: κακῶς means badly or wrongly. The ἵνα clause says what is wrong: they ask so that they can spend what they receive on their pleasures (ἡδοναῖς, the word of verse 1). Prayer is turned into a way of feeding the desires that cause the fighting.

decisions.choice: spend: use up, consume
decisions.reason: δαπανάω is to spend or use up, as the younger son spent everything he had (Luke 15:14).

decisions.choice: when you do ask; ask God; for the wrong reasons; only
alternatives: You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable link this sentence to the last one ("you do not ask") and say what the wrong asking is (m2). Readable names God as the one asked (as in verse 2) and "only" brings out the selfish aim.

source.text: μοιχαλίδες, οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: Adulteresses, not you know that the friendship of the world hostility of the God is?

en.L: Adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God?
en.B: Adulterous people! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God?
en.R: You are like a wife who is unfaithful to her husband! Do you not know that being a friend of the world makes you an enemy of God?

es.L: Adúlteras, ¿no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que la amistad del mundo es hostilidad hacia Dios?
es.B: ¡Gente adúltera! ¿No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que la amistad con el mundo es enemistad con Dios?
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como una esposa que le es infiel a su marido! ¿No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que ser amigos del mundo {{plural_you:los|os}} convierte en enemigos de Dios?

sw.L: Enyi wanawake wazinzi, hamjui kwamba urafiki wa ulimwengu ni uadui na Mungu?
sw.B: Enyi watu wazinzi! Je, hamjui kwamba urafiki na ulimwengu ni uadui dhidi ya Mungu?
sw.R: Mko kama mke asiye mwaminifu kwa mume wake! Je, hamjui kwamba kuwa rafiki wa ulimwengu kunawafanya kuwa maadui wa Mungu?

decisions.choice: adulteresses: God's people pictured as a wife unfaithful to her husband
decisions.reason: The feminine plural μοιχαλίδες takes up the prophets' picture of Israel as God's wife who goes after other lovers (Hosea 2-3; Jeremiah 3:20; Ezekiel 16). Jesus speaks of "an adulterous generation" (Matthew 12:39). The unfaithfulness here is friendship with the world, not a sexual sin, and the word applies to men and women alike.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "adulteresses" alone
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the masculine "adulterers and" before "adulteresses", probably because copyists took the word literally and wanted to include men. Older manuscripts and the SBLGNT have the feminine alone, which suits the picture of an unfaithful wife (m1). This note is written from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the world: human life ordered without God and against him
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is not the created world but the way of life opposed to God, as in 1:27 ("unstained by the world"). To be its friend is to share its values: the selfish desires of verses 1-3.

decisions.choice: hostility toward God
decisions.reason: ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ is hostility directed at God. Friendship and hostility are set against each other: there is no neutral ground between the two.

decisions.choice: Adulterous people; like a wife who is unfaithful to her husband
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the feminine plural. Balanced makes it a description of the readers, and Readable explains the picture (m1), since "adulteresses" alone would suggest that the readers are women who have committed adultery.

decisions.choice: Enyi wanawake wazinzi
decisions.reason: Swahili nouns do not mark gender, so "wazinzi" alone would lose the feminine form of the Greek word and with it the picture of an unfaithful wife (m1). Literal adds "wanawake" to keep it, as the English Literal keeps "adulteresses". Balanced and Readable follow the English ("watu wazinzi"; "mke asiye mwaminifu").

source.text: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου, ἐχθρὸς τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσταται.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever if therefore chooses a friend to be of the world, an enemy of the God is made.

en.L: Whoever therefore chooses to be a friend of the world is made an enemy of God.
en.B: So whoever decides to be a friend of the world is taking a stand as an enemy of God.
en.R: So if you choose to be the world's friend, you are making yourself an enemy of God.

es.L: Así pues, quien elija ser amigo del mundo se vuelve enemigo de Dios.
es.B: Así que el que decide ser amigo del mundo se declara enemigo de Dios.
es.R: Así que, si {{plural_you:eligen|elegís}} ser amigos del mundo, {{plural_you:se están|os estáis}} haciendo enemigos de Dios.

sw.L: Basi yeyote atakayetaka kuwa rafiki wa ulimwengu, anafanywa adui wa Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo yeyote anayeamua kuwa rafiki wa ulimwengu anajiweka kuwa adui wa Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mkichagua kuwa marafiki wa ulimwengu, mnajifanya kuwa maadui wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: chooses: sets the will on, decides
decisions.reason: βούλομαι is to want or intend. It is a deliberate choice, not a slip.

decisions.choice: is made an enemy: takes the place of an enemy by that choice
alternatives: is appointed an enemy by God
decisions.reason: καθίσταται can be passive ("is appointed") or middle ("sets himself up as"). Since the sentence is about what a person chooses, the sense is that by that choice the person takes the place of an enemy of God.

decisions.choice: is taking a stand as; making yourself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the person takes this place by choice (m2). Literal keeps the open form "is made". Readable speaks to "you", as James does in the sentence before.

decisions.choice: se vuelve
decisions.reason: Spanish "se vuelve" (becomes) does not say whether the person is made an enemy or makes himself one, so Literal keeps the Greek form open, as the English "is made" does (m2). Balanced "se declara" brings out the choice.

source.text: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Or you think that in vain the Scripture says, With envy yearns the spirit that he made to dwell in us?

en.L: Or do you think that the Scripture speaks in vain: "[He] longs with jealousy for the spirit that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to dwell in us"?
en.B: Or do you suppose that Scripture speaks for nothing when it says, "He longs with jealous love for the spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} caused to live in us"?
en.R: Do you think Scripture means nothing when it says, "God jealously wants the spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put in us for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}"?

es.L: ¿O {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que la Escritura dice en vano: «[Él] anhela con celos el espíritu que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo habitar en nosotros»?
es.B: ¿O {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} que la Escritura habla sin motivo cuando dice: «Él anhela con amor celoso el espíritu que hizo vivir en nosotros»?
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Creen|Creéis}} que la Escritura no quiere decir nada cuando dice: «Dios desea con celo que el espíritu que puso en nosotros sea solo para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}»?

sw.L: Au mnadhani kwamba Maandiko yanasema bure: "Kwa wivu anaitamani roho aliyoifanya ikae ndani yetu"?
sw.B: Au mnadhani kwamba Maandiko yanasema bila maana yanaposema, "Anaitamani kwa upendo wenye wivu roho aliyoiweka ikae ndani yetu"?
sw.R: Je, mnadhani Maandiko hayana maana yanaposema, "Mungu anaitaka kwa wivu roho aliyoiweka ndani yetu iwe mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tu"?

decisions.choice: God is the one who longs; the spirit is what he longs for
alternatives: the spirit God made to dwell in us longs enviously: the human spirit is prone to envy
the Spirit God made to dwell in us longs jealously over us
decisions.reason: τὸ πνεῦμα can be the subject or the object of ἐπιποθεῖ. God is the subject of "made to dwell", and taking God as the subject of "longs" as well keeps one subject through the sentence. It fits the context: the readers have just been called unfaithful (verse 4), and God's jealous claim on his people runs through Scripture (Exodus 20:5; 34:14; Deuteronomy 32:16). On the other side, φθόνος elsewhere means envy, a vice (Galatians 5:21; Titus 3:3), which suits a sentence about a human spirit that tends toward envy, like the envy of verse 2.

decisions.choice: with jealousy: the jealous love of God for those who belong to him
decisions.reason: Πρὸς φθόνον is an adverbial phrase: "enviously" or "jealously". Applied to God it means his claim on his people, who may not share their love with the world. This sense is unusual for this word, which is why some prefer the reading in which the spirit is the subject (m1).

decisions.choice: Scripture says: no Old Testament verse has these words
alternatives: "Scripture says" introduces the quotation in verse 6
a quotation from a writing now lost
decisions.reason: The words after "Scripture says" are not found in any Old Testament book. They may sum up what Scripture teaches about God's jealous love (Exodus 20:5; 34:14; Zechariah 8:2), or quote a writing that has not survived. Some take "Scripture says" with the quotation of Proverbs 3:34 in verse 6 and read the rest of verse 5 as a separate question. The SBLGNT's capital letter marks what follows as the words quoted.

decisions.choice: the spirit: the life God placed in human beings
decisions.reason: God "made to dwell" the spirit in us. This may be the breath of life God breathed into the first man (Genesis 2:7; Ecclesiastes 12:7), or the Holy Spirit given to believers. The sentence does not settle which, and the main point is the same: God claims what he has given.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: κατῴκισεν, "made to dwell"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a verb that differs by one letter and means "dwelt", which makes the spirit the one who dwells: "the spirit that dwells in us". Older manuscripts and the SBLGNT have "made to dwell", with God as the subject. This note is written from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God; for himself
alternatives: he yearns jealously over the spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who longs (m1) and says what his jealous longing wants. This follows a reading that is not certain.

decisions.choice: the spirit (lowercase)
decisions.reason: A lowercase "spirit" leaves open whether the human spirit or the Holy Spirit is meant (m4).

decisions.choice: celos; amor celoso; con celo
decisions.reason: "Envidia" is resentment of what others have, the sense of verse 2 ("envidian"). "Celos" is the jealousy of love that will not share the one it loves, which fits God's claim on his people (m2).

decisions.choice: wivu
decisions.reason: Swahili "wivu" covers both envy and jealous love, and is the word used of God's jealousy ("Mungu mwenye wivu"). Verse 2 uses it for envy ("mnaona wivu"); here Balanced makes plain that it is love that claims ("upendo wenye wivu"). As in Romans, the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("mali yake"); pronouns inside the verb ("aliyoiweka") have none.

source.text: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν· διὸ λέγει· Ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν.

records.literal_gloss: Greater but he gives grace; therefore it says, The God proud [ones] opposes, humble [ones] but gives grace.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives greater grace; therefore it says, "God sets {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} against [the] proud, but gives grace to [the] humble."
en.B: But the grace {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives is greater. That is why it says, "God sets {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} against the proud, but to the humble {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace."
en.R: But God gives us even more grace. That is why Scripture says, "God fights against people who are proud, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace to people who are humble."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da mayor gracia; por eso dice: «Dios se opone a [los] soberbios, pero da gracia a [los] humildes».
es.B: Pero la gracia que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da es mayor. Por eso dice: «Dios se pone en contra de los soberbios, pero a los humildes les da gracia».
es.R: Pero Dios nos da todavía más gracia. Por eso la Escritura dice: «Dios lucha contra los orgullosos, pero a los humildes les da gracia».

sw.L: Lakini anatoa neema kubwa zaidi; kwa hiyo inasema: "Mungu anajipanga dhidi ya wenye kiburi, lakini wanyenyekevu anawapa neema."
sw.B: Lakini neema anayoitoa ni kubwa zaidi. Ndiyo maana inasema, "Mungu anasimama dhidi ya wenye kiburi, lakini wanyenyekevu anawapa neema."
sw.R: Lakini Mungu anatupa neema zaidi tena. Ndiyo maana Maandiko yanasema, "Mungu anapigana na watu wenye kiburi, lakini anawapa neema watu wanyenyekevu."

decisions.choice: greater grace: grace stronger than the pull of the world and of envy
decisions.reason: μείζονα is a comparative: "greater". After the hard demand of verses 4-5, James says that God gives more than he demands: grace stronger than the desires at war within (verse 1).

decisions.choice: Proverbs 3:34, in its Greek form
decisions.reason: James quotes Proverbs 3:34 as it stands in the Greek translation of the Old Testament, with "God" where that translation has "Lord". 1 Peter 5:5 quotes the same verse. The Hebrew says that he mocks the mockers but shows favor to the humble.

decisions.choice: it says: Scripture says
decisions.reason: The subject of λέγει is not stated. After "Scripture says" in verse 5, the natural subject is Scripture; its words are God's words.

decisions.choice: sets himself against: opposes, as one army is drawn up against another
decisions.reason: ἀντιτάσσομαι is a military word, "to line up against". It answers the war language of verses 1-2: the proud are at war with God himself.

decisions.choice: God gives us even more grace; Scripture says
alternatives: he gives greater grace; it says
decisions.reason: Readable names the giver and the speaker (m3).

decisions.choice: anajipanga dhidi ya
decisions.reason: "Kujipanga" is to draw up in line, as troops do, so Literal keeps the military picture of the verb (m4). Balanced says "anasimama dhidi ya" (stands against), Readable "anapigana na" (fights).

source.text: ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ θεῷ· ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ, καὶ φεύξεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Be subject therefore to the God; resist but the devil, and he will flee from you;

en.L: Be subject therefore to God; but stand against the devil, and he will flee from you.
en.B: So place yourselves under God. Stand against the devil, and he will run from you.
en.R: So let God be the one who rules over you. Stand up against the devil, and he will run away from you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sométanse|Someteos}}, pues, a Dios; pero {{plural_you:resistan|resistid}} al diablo, y huirá de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} bajo el mando de Dios. {{plural_you:Háganle|Hacedle}} frente al diablo, y huirá de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que Dios sea quien gobierne {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida. {{plural_you:Enfréntense|Enfrentaos}} al diablo, y él huirá lejos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Jiwekeni chini ya Mungu, basi; lakini simameni kinyume na Ibilisi, naye atakimbia kutoka kwenu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo jiwekeni chini ya Mungu. Simameni imara dhidi ya Ibilisi, naye atakimbia mbali nanyi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mwacheni Mungu awe mtawala wenu. Simameni kidete dhidi ya Ibilisi, naye atawaacha na kukimbia.

decisions.choice: be subject: take your place under God's authority
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσω is to place under, a word of rank and order. The command calls them to accept their place under God, the humble stance of the proverb just quoted (verse 6), and οὖν draws the conclusion from it. It opens a run of commands in verses 7-10, a call to turn back to God now.

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, the enemy of God
decisions.reason: διάβολος means slanderer. James has called the "wisdom" of jealousy and ambition demonic (3:15). Yielding to God and standing against the devil are two sides of one turning, with the same promise as 1 Peter 5:8-9.

decisions.choice: resist: stand firm against
decisions.reason: ἀνθίστημι is to take a stand against an opponent (Ephesians 6:13). It is the same stance God takes toward the proud in verse 6, now taken by the humble toward the devil.

decisions.choice: place yourselves under; let God be the one who rules over you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of rank in the Greek word; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: Ibilisi
decisions.reason: The Greek word here means the slanderer, the devil (m2). "Ibilisi" is the Swahili word for the devil; "Shetani" is kept for the name Satan.

source.text: ἐγγίσατε τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Draw near to the God, and he will draw near to you.

en.L: Draw close to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will draw close to you.
en.B: Draw close to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will draw close to you.
en.R: Get close to God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will get close to you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}} a Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se acercará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}} a Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se acercará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}} a Dios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se acercará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Njooni karibu na Mungu, naye atakuja karibu nanyi.
sw.B: Jongeeni karibu na Mungu, naye atajongea karibu nanyi.
sw.R: Sogeeni karibu na Mungu, naye atasogea karibu nanyi.

decisions.choice: draw near: the language of worship and of returning to God
decisions.reason: ἐγγίζω is used of priests who come near to God (Exodus 19:22). The promise that God will come near to those who come near echoes the prophets' call: "Return to me, and I will return to you" (Zechariah 1:3; Malachi 3:7).

decisions.choice: not a price paid for God's favor, but the response of the humble to his grace
decisions.reason: The command stands within verses 6-10, which begin with God giving greater grace to the humble. Coming near is how the humble receive what God already offers.

source.text: καθαρίσατε χεῖρας, ἁμαρτωλοί, καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας, δίψυχοι.

records.literal_gloss: Cleanse hands, sinners, and purify hearts, double-minded.

en.L: Cleanse [your] hands, sinners, and purify [your] hearts, double-minded [ones].
en.B: Wash your hands clean, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you who are divided in mind.
en.R: You sinners, clean up what your hands do. You who are divided between God and the world, make your hearts pure.

es.L: {{plural_you:Limpien|Limpiad}} [las] manos, pecadores, y {{plural_you:purifiquen|purificad}} [los] corazones, [los] de doble ánimo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Lávense|Lavaos}} las manos, pecadores, y {{plural_you:purifiquen|purificad}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} divididos por dentro.
es.R: Pecadores, {{plural_you:limpien|limpiad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} acciones. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} divididos entre Dios y el mundo, {{plural_you:purifiquen|purificad}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón.

sw.L: Safisheni mikono [yenu], enyi watenda dhambi, na takaseni mioyo [yenu], enyi wenye nia mbili.
sw.B: Osheni mikono yenu iwe safi, enyi watenda dhambi, na mfanye mioyo yenu iwe safi, ninyi wenye nia mbili.
sw.R: Enyi watenda dhambi, safisheni matendo ya mikono yenu. Ninyi mnaogawanyika kati ya Mungu na ulimwengu, fanyeni mioyo yenu iwe safi.

decisions.choice: clean hands and a pure heart: Psalm 24:3-4
decisions.reason: The psalm asks who may stand in God's holy place: the one with clean hands and a pure heart. Hands stand for what a person does, the heart for what a person wants. The washing language comes from the rules for priests approaching God (Exodus 30:19-21), which fits "draw near" just before.

decisions.choice: double-minded: divided in loyalty between God and the world
decisions.reason: δίψυχος, literally "two-souled", was used in 1:8 of someone who prays while doubting. Here it is the divided loyalty of verse 4: wanting to be a friend of the world and of God.

decisions.choice: purify: make clean for God
decisions.reason: ἁγνίζω is used of the purification before a festival (John 11:55) and of moral cleansing (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:3). Here it is the heart, not the body, that must be made clean.

decisions.choice: clean up what your hands do; divided between God and the world
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hands stand for (m1) and what the divided mind is divided between (m2).

decisions.choice: de doble ánimo (L); divididos por dentro (B)
decisions.reason: "De doble ánimo" is the settled Literal term for this word in James. Balanced says what it means in plain Spanish, and Readable names the two sides (m2).

decisions.choice: wenye nia mbili
decisions.reason: "Mwenye nia mbili" (having two minds) is the settled term for this word in James, as in 1:8. Readable says what the two sides are (m2).

source.text: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε· ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν·

records.literal_gloss: Be wretched and mourn and weep; the laughter of you into mourning let be turned and the joy into gloom;

en.L: Be wretched and mourn and weep; let your laughter be turned into mourning and [your] joy into gloom.
en.B: Feel your misery, and mourn and weep. Let your laughter turn to mourning and your joy to gloom.
en.R: Be truly sorry for your sins. Grieve and cry. Let your laughing turn into crying, and your joy into sadness.

es.L: {{plural_you:Aflíjanse|Afligíos}} y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}; que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} risa se convierta en duelo y [{{plural_you:su|vuestro}}] gozo en abatimiento.
es.B: {{plural_you:Reconozcan|Reconoced}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} miseria, y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}. Que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} risa se vuelva duelo, y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} gozo, abatimiento.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sientan|Sentid}} de verdad dolor por {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados. {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} tristes y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}. Que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} risa se convierta en llanto, y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alegría en tristeza.

sw.L: Taabikeni na ombolezeni na lieni; kicheko chenu kibadilike kuwa maombolezo, na furaha [yenu] kuwa simanzi.
sw.B: Tambueni unyonge wenu, mkaomboleze na kulia. Kicheko chenu kibadilike kuwa maombolezo, na furaha yenu iwe simanzi.
sw.R: Jutieni kweli dhambi zenu. Ombolezeni na kulia. Acheni kicheko chenu kigeuke kuwa kilio, na furaha yenu kuwa huzuni.

decisions.choice: be wretched: feel and show the misery of your state before God
decisions.reason: ταλαιπωρέω means to be miserable or distressed. As a command it calls them to see how wretched their state is. A related word appears in Romans 7:24 and in James 5:1, of the miseries coming on the rich.

decisions.choice: the mourning of repentance, not a ban on all joy
alternatives: sorrow as a lasting way of life
decisions.reason: The commands echo the prophets' call to return to God with weeping and mourning (Joel 2:12-13). The laughter and joy are those of people careless about their sin (Luke 6:25), not the joy James commands in trials (1:2). χαρὰ is the same word as in 1:2; what changes is what the joy is in.

decisions.choice: gloom: a downcast face
decisions.reason: κατήφεια is dejection: the look of someone whose eyes are lowered in shame.

decisions.choice: Be truly sorry for your sins
decisions.reason: Readable says what the misery is about (m2).

decisions.choice: simanzi
decisions.reason: "Simanzi" is a heavy, downcast sorrow that shows on the face, close to the meaning decision's "downcast face" (m3). Readable uses the everyday "huzuni".

source.text: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον κυρίου, καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Be humbled before [the] Lord, and he will exalt you.

en.L: Be humbled in the presence of [the] Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise you high.
en.B: Make yourselves low before the Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise you high.
en.R: Be humble in front of the Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lift you up to a place of honor.

es.L: {{plural_you:Humíllense|Humillaos}} en presencia del Señor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} levantará en alto.
es.B: {{plural_you:Háganse|Haceos}} pequeños delante del Señor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} levantará en alto.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} humildes ante el Señor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} pondrá en un lugar de honor.

sw.L: Mnyenyekezwe mbele ya Bwana, naye atawainua juu.
sw.B: Jishusheni chini mbele ya Bwana, naye atawainua juu.
sw.R: Kuweni wanyenyekevu mbele ya Bwana, naye atawainua na kuwapa heshima.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: In verses 6-10 the one who gives grace to the humble is God, and "Lord" takes up the same subject (as in 1:7). James also calls Jesus Lord (1:1; 2:1), so the reference is not certain, but the parallel with verse 7 ("be subject to God") points to God.

decisions.choice: the humble raised: Proverbs 3:34 again, and the reversal of 1:9
decisions.reason: This closes the call begun in verse 6, where God gives grace to the humble. Jesus said that whoever humbles himself will be exalted (Luke 14:11; 18:14). James promised the same to the brother of low position in 1:9.

decisions.choice: be humbled: humble yourselves
decisions.reason: ταπεινώθητε is passive in form, but as a command it calls for something they do: take the low place before God.

decisions.choice: make yourselves low; raise you high; lift you up to a place of honor
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of low and high in the two verbs. Readable says what being raised means.

source.text: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων, ἀδελφοί· ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον· εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις, οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής.

records.literal_gloss: Not speak against one another, brothers; the [one] speaking against a brother or judging the brother of him speaks against law and judges law; if but law you judge, not you are a doer of law but a judge.

en.L: Do not speak against one another, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. The [one] speaking against {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} or judging {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} speaks against law and judges law; but if you judge law, you are not a doer of law but a judge.
en.B: Do not speak against one another, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. Whoever speaks against {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} or passes judgment on {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} speaks against the law and judges the law. And if you judge the law, you are not doing the law; you are judging it.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, do not say evil things about one another. When you speak against a fellow believer or judge them, you are speaking against God's law and judging it. And if you judge the law, you are not obeying it. You are making yourself its judge.

es.L: No {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} mal unos de otros, hermanos. El que habla mal de un hermano o juzga a su hermano, habla mal de [la] ley y juzga [la] ley; pero si juzgas [la] ley, no eres hacedor de [la] ley, sino juez.
es.B: Hermanos, no {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} mal unos de otros. Quien habla mal de un hermano o juzga a un hermano, habla mal de la ley y juzga a la ley. Y si juzgas a la ley, no estás cumpliendo la ley, sino que te haces su juez.
es.R: Hermanos, no {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} cosas malas unos de otros. Cuando hablas mal de otro creyente o lo juzgas, estás hablando mal de la ley de Dios y la estás juzgando. Y si juzgas la ley, no la estás obedeciendo. Te estás haciendo su juez.

sw.L: Msisemane vibaya, ndugu. Anayemsema vibaya ndugu au kumhukumu ndugu yake, anaisema vibaya sheria na kuihukumu sheria; lakini kama unaihukumu sheria, wewe si mtendaji wa sheria bali ni mwamuzi.
sw.B: Ndugu, msisemane vibaya. Mtu anayemsema vibaya ndugu au kumhukumu ndugu, anaisema vibaya sheria na kuihukumu sheria. Na kama unaihukumu sheria, huitendi sheria; unaihukumu.
sw.R: Ndugu, msiseme mabaya juu ya wenzenu. Unapomsema vibaya mwamini mwenzako au kumhukumu, unaisema vibaya sheria ya Mungu na kuihukumu. Na ukiihukumu sheria, huitii. Unajifanya kuwa mwamuzi wake.

decisions.choice: speak against: run someone down with words, slander
decisions.reason: καταλαλέω is to speak against someone, often behind their back (1 Peter 2:12; 3:16). After chapter 3 on the tongue, James names one of its commonest sins.

decisions.choice: the law: the law of love that James called the royal law
decisions.reason: The law in view is the one James quoted in 2:8, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself" (Leviticus 19:18). Just before it, Leviticus 19:16 forbids going about as a slanderer among one's people. Verse 12 speaks of "the neighbor", the word of that commandment.

decisions.choice: to judge the law is to put oneself above it
decisions.reason: The one who slanders acts as if the law of love did not apply, and so passes judgment on the law itself. But the readers' calling is to be doers of the law (1:22-25; 2:8), not its judges; there is only one Judge (verse 12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}}
decisions.reason: The singular ἀδελφός here stands for any fellow believer, man or woman. The traditional form is the alternative.

decisions.choice: a fellow believer; God's law; not obeying it
alternatives: a brother; law; not a doer of law
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "brother" is, whose law is meant (m2), and what being a doer of the law means.

decisions.choice: hermanos; un hermano; no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, and the singular "un hermano" here stands for any fellow believer, so the Spanish has no gender span. For review: a reviewer may prefer "un hermano o una hermana" for the singular.

decisions.choice: tú
decisions.reason: James turns to one imagined hearer with singular verbs ("if you judge" here, "who are you" in verse 12), so Spanish uses "tú" there with no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" is a brother or a sister, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili, here or elsewhere in the chapter.

source.text: εἷς ἐστιν νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής, ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι· σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ, ὁ κρίνων τὸν πλησίον;

records.literal_gloss: One is lawgiver and judge, the [one] being able to save and to destroy; you but who are you, the [one] judging the neighbor?

en.L: One is Lawgiver and Judge, the [one] able to save and to destroy; but you, who are you, the [one] judging the neighbor?
en.B: There is one Lawgiver and Judge alone, the one who has power to save and to destroy. But you, who are you to sit in judgment on your neighbor?
en.R: Only God gives the law and judges by it. He is able to save and to destroy. So who do you think you are, judging your neighbor?

es.L: Uno [solo] es [el] Legislador y Juez, el que puede salvar y destruir; pero tú, ¿quién eres, el que juzga al prójimo?
es.B: Hay un solo Legislador y Juez, el que tiene poder para salvar y para destruir. Pero tú, ¿quién eres para juzgar a tu prójimo?
es.R: Solo Dios da la ley y juzga según ella. Él puede salvar y destruir. Así que, ¿quién te crees que eres para juzgar a tu prójimo?

sw.L: Mmoja ndiye Mweka Sheria na Mwamuzi, yule anayeweza kuokoa na kuangamiza; lakini wewe, wewe ni nani, unayemhukumu jirani?
sw.B: Kuna Mweka Sheria na Mwamuzi mmoja tu, yule mwenye uwezo wa kuokoa na kuangamiza. Lakini wewe ni nani hata umhukumu jirani yako?
sw.R: Mungu peke yake ndiye anayetoa sheria na kuhukumu kwa sheria hiyo. Yeye anaweza kuokoa na kuangamiza. Basi wewe unadhani wewe ni nani, hata umhukumu jirani yako?

decisions.choice: one: God alone
decisions.reason: εἷς echoes the confession that God is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), which James quoted in 2:19. The one who gave the law is the one who will judge by it (Isaiah 33:22), and he alone has power over life and death (Deuteronomy 32:39; Matthew 10:28). In 5:9 the Judge stands at the door, where the coming Lord may be meant.

decisions.choice: save and destroy: the two outcomes of the final judgment
decisions.reason: σῴζω and ἀπόλλυμι name the outcomes of the last judgment, as "save" does in 1:21 and 2:14.

decisions.choice: who are you: a rebuke
decisions.reason: The emphatic σὺ sets the one who judges a neighbor against the one true Judge: a human being has taken God's place.

decisions.choice: Only God; He is able
alternatives: There is one Lawgiver and Judge
decisions.reason: Readable names the One (m1).

source.text: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες· Σήμερον ἢ αὔριον πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ κερδήσομεν·

records.literal_gloss: Come now, the [ones] saying: Today or tomorrow we will go into this the city and we will spend there a year and we will trade and we will make a profit;

en.L: Come now, [you] who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to such-and-such a city, and we will spend a year there, and we will trade, and we will make a profit."
en.B: Listen now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will travel to a certain city, stay there a year, run a business, and make a profit."
en.R: Listen, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this city or that one. We will stay there for a year. We will buy and sell and make money."

es.L: ¡Vamos ahora, los que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Hoy o mañana iremos a tal ciudad, y pasaremos allí un año, y comerciaremos, y obtendremos ganancia»!
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} ahora, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Hoy o mañana viajaremos a cierta ciudad, nos quedaremos allí un año, haremos negocios y sacaremos ganancias».
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «Hoy o mañana iremos a esta o aquella ciudad. Nos quedaremos allí un año. Compraremos y venderemos, y ganaremos dinero».

sw.L: Njooni sasa, ninyi mnaosema, "Leo au kesho tutasafiri kwenda mji fulani, na tutakaa huko mwaka mmoja, na tutafanya biashara, na tutachuma faida."
sw.B: Sikilizeni sasa, ninyi mnaosema, "Leo au kesho tutasafiri kwenda mji fulani, tutakaa huko mwaka mmoja, tutaendesha biashara na kuchuma faida."
sw.R: Sikilizeni, ninyi mnaosema, "Leo au kesho tutakwenda mji huu au ule. Tutakaa huko kwa mwaka mmoja. Tutanunua na kuuza na kupata pesa."

decisions.choice: come now: a sharp call to attention
decisions.reason: Ἄγε νῦν calls hearers to listen. James uses it again in 5:1, to the rich. It opens a new section.

decisions.choice: travelling merchants planning a season of trade
decisions.reason: Trade meant travel between cities and staying long enough to buy and sell. James does not condemn trade, but planning as if the future were in one's own hands (verses 14-16). Proverbs 27:1 warns: do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on through verse 15, with verse 14 as a remark in between
decisions.reason: οἵτινες in verse 14 and ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν in verse 15 both depend on "you who say" here. Verse 15 tells them what they should say instead.

decisions.choice: Listen now; Listen
decisions.reason: "Come now" is a call to attention, not an invitation to come (m1). Balanced and Readable use the word that does that job today.

decisions.choice: this city or that one; buy and sell and make money
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "such-and-such a city" and "trade" in everyday words.

source.text: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε τὸ τῆς αὔριον ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν· ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστε ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη·

records.literal_gloss: who not know the [thing] of tomorrow, what kind the life of you; a mist for you are that for a little [while] appears, then also vanishes;

en.L: [Yet] you do not know the [matter] of tomorrow, what your life [will be] like; for you are a mist that appears for a little [while], then also vanishes.
en.B: Yet you do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. You are a puff of vapor, seen for a short time and then gone.
en.R: But you cannot tell how your life will go tomorrow. You are like a mist. People see it for a little while, and then it is gone.

es.L: [Pero] no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo de mañana, cómo [será] {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida; porque {{plural_you:son|sois}} un vapor que aparece por poco [tiempo] y después también desaparece.
es.B: Pero no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} cómo será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida mañana. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} un soplo de vapor que se ve por un momento y luego desaparece.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} saber cómo {{plural_you:les|os}} irá en la vida mañana. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como la neblina. La gente la ve un rato, y luego ya no está.

sw.L: [Lakini] hamjui ya kesho, maisha yenu [yatakuwa] ya namna gani; kwa maana ninyi ni ukungu unaoonekana kwa kitambo kidogo, kisha nao unatoweka.
sw.B: Lakini hamjui maisha yenu yatakuwaje kesho. Ninyi ni ukungu unaoonekana kwa muda mfupi, kisha unapotea.
sw.R: Lakini hamwezi kujua maisha yenu yatakwendaje kesho. Ninyi ni kama ukungu. Watu wanauona kwa muda kidogo, kisha haupo tena.

decisions.choice: you do not know what your life will be like tomorrow
alternatives: "You do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates this as one statement: they do not know tomorrow's matter, what their life will be like. Other editions put a question mark after "tomorrow" and read "What is your life?" as a question of its own. The point is the same: tomorrow, and life itself, are not in their hands.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "for you are a mist"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in small ways in this verse: some have a plural article ("the things of tomorrow"), some lack "for", and many read "it is a mist", with life as the subject. The SBLGNT reads "you are". The meaning is not changed. This note is written from general knowledge of the manuscripts and must be checked against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: mist: vapor or smoke that soon disappears
decisions.reason: ἀτμίς is steam, vapor or smoke (Acts 2:19, quoting Joel 2:30). Scripture often pictures human life as breath or smoke (Psalm 39:5; 102:3; Job 7:7).

decisions.choice: a new sentence
decisions.reason: οἵτινες, "you who", carries on the sentence from verse 13. All three levels start a new sentence here, with "Yet" or "But" for the link; Literal brackets the added word.

decisions.choice: You are like a mist. People see it
alternatives: you are a mist that appears
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison plain and gives "appears" a subject.

decisions.choice: maisha
decisions.reason: "Uzima" is life itself, the word for eternal life; "maisha" is the course of a person's life from day to day. James asks what their life will be like tomorrow, so "maisha" fits.

source.text: ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς· Ἐὰν ὁ κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο.

records.literal_gloss: Instead of the to say you: If the Lord wills, both we will live and we will do this or that.

en.L: Instead of your saying, "If the Lord wills, we will both live and do this or that."
en.B: What you ought to say instead is this: "If the Lord wills, we will live, and we will do this or that."
en.R: Instead, this is what you should say: "If the Lord wants it, we will live, and we will do this or that."

es.L: En lugar de que {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: «Si el Señor quiere, tanto viviremos como haremos esto o aquello».
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} decir, más bien, es esto: «Si el Señor lo quiere, viviremos, y haremos esto o aquello».
es.R: En vez de eso, esto es lo que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} decir: «Si el Señor así lo quiere, viviremos y haremos esto o aquello».

sw.L: Badala ya ninyi kusema, "Bwana akitaka, tutaishi, na tena tutafanya hili au lile."
sw.B: Mnachopaswa kusema badala yake ni hiki: "Bwana akitaka, tutaishi, na tutafanya hili au lile."
sw.R: Badala yake, mnapaswa kusema hivi: "Ikiwa Bwana anataka, tutaishi, na tutafanya hili au lile."

decisions.choice: instead of saying: this continues verse 13, after the remark of verse 14
decisions.reason: ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν depends on "you who say" in verse 13: they say "Today or tomorrow we will go", instead of saying "If the Lord wills".

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose will governs life and plans
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, "the Lord" is most likely God, whose will decides the future (Acts 18:21; 1 Corinthians 4:19). James also calls Jesus Lord, so the reference cannot be settled from this verse alone.

decisions.choice: both live and do: the "if" covers being alive as well as doing
alternatives: If the Lord wills and we live, we will do this or that
decisions.reason: καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν makes both verbs depend on the Lord's will: even being alive tomorrow is in God's hands, not only the success of the plan.

decisions.choice: What you ought to say instead is this; Instead, this is what you should say
decisions.reason: The Greek phrase hangs on verse 13 (m1). Balanced and Readable, which start a new sentence, supply the "ought" it implies.

source.text: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν· πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Now but you boast in the arrogances of you; all boasting such evil is.

en.L: But now you boast in your arrogant [claims]; all boasting of this sort is evil.
en.B: But as things are, you boast in your arrogant claims. Every boast of this kind is evil.
en.R: But instead, you are proud and you brag about your plans. All bragging like this is evil.

es.L: Pero ahora {{plural_you:se jactan|os jactáis}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} [pretensiones] arrogantes; toda jactancia de esta clase es mala.
es.B: Pero tal como están las cosas, {{plural_you:se jactan|os jactáis}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} pretensiones arrogantes. Toda jactancia así es mala.
es.R: Pero en lugar de eso, {{plural_you:son|sois}} orgullosos y {{plural_you:presumen|presumís}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} planes. Presumir así es malo.

sw.L: Lakini sasa mnajigamba katika [maneno yenu ya] kiburi; majigambo yote ya namna hii ni maovu.
sw.B: Lakini hali ilivyo, mnajigamba kwa madai yenu ya kiburi. Majigambo yote ya namna hii ni maovu.
sw.R: Lakini badala yake, mna kiburi na mnajigamba juu ya mipango yenu. Kujigamba kwa namna hii ni uovu.

decisions.choice: arrogant claims: proud talk about what one will do
decisions.reason: ἀλαζονεία is the bragging of someone who claims more than he has or can do; 1 John 2:16 uses it of the pride in one's possessions. The plural points to the boastful plans just quoted (verse 13).

decisions.choice: but now: as things actually are
decisions.reason: νῦν δὲ sets what they do against what they should say (verse 15). It is not "now" in time but "as it is".

decisions.choice: boasting of this sort is evil: boasting that leaves God out
decisions.reason: James does not condemn all boasting; he tells the lowly to boast in being raised up (1:9). καύχησις τοιαύτη, "such boasting", is the kind that speaks of the future as one's own (Proverbs 27:1; Jeremiah 9:23-24).

decisions.choice: you are proud and you brag about your plans
decisions.reason: Readable says what the arrogant claims are (m1).

source.text: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι, ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: To [one] knowing therefore good to do and not doing, sin to him it is.

en.L: So to [the one] who knows to do good and does not do [it], to {{gender:that person|him}} it is sin.
en.B: So when someone knows what is good to do and does not do it, that person sins.
en.R: So if you know the good thing you should do, and you do not do it, you are sinning.

es.L: Así pues, a quien sabe hacer el bien y no [lo] hace, [eso] le es pecado.
es.B: Así que, cuando alguien sabe el bien que debe hacer y no lo hace, peca.
es.R: Así que, si {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} qué es lo bueno que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} hacer, y no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pecando.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mtu anayejua kufanya jema na halifanyi, kwake hilo ni dhambi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo mtu akijua jema analopaswa kufanya, na asilifanye, anatenda dhambi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mkijua jambo jema mnalopaswa kufanya, na hamlifanyi, mnatenda dhambi.

decisions.choice: so: a closing saying, applied to what comes before
decisions.reason: οὖν links the saying to verses 13-16: they know they should say "If the Lord wills", and not doing so is sin. It also sums up the letter's call to be doers and not only hearers (1:22-25; 2:14-17).

decisions.choice: sin includes failing to do the good one knows
decisions.reason: Sin is not only doing what is forbidden but leaving undone the good one knows to do (Luke 12:47; compare the one who sees someone in need and does nothing, 2:15-16).

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}}
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ refers to anyone who knows the good, man or woman. The traditional masculine is the alternative.

decisions.choice: you
alternatives: the one who knows; to him
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the reader directly, as James does in verses 13-16.

decisions.choice: le, no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "le" refers to a man or a woman, so the English gender setting on "him" has nothing to change in Spanish.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the readers directly, as the English Readable does, and in the plural, as James does in verses 13-16; so the verbs carry the ustedes/vosotros setting.
